**Incident Overview**

On March 12, 2025, a fairness audit found that the CreditScore-ML v4.2 loan approval system was denying applications from Hispanic applicants at a rate 23% higher than non-Hispanic applicants who had similar credit qualifications. The system had been in use for 11 months without a fairness review. Applicants who were denied did not know an automated system made the decision and had no way to appeal. This incident is rated **Critical** severity.

**Root Cause**

The system was trained on 15 years of historical loan data that reflected past discriminatory lending practices. Features such as zip code and employment sector acted as proxies for race, causing the system to reproduce those discriminatory patterns. No disparate impact testing—analysis to detect whether a system treats protected groups unfairly—was conducted before the system went live.

**Remediation Steps**

1. Suspend the model immediately and route all new loan decisions to human underwriters.
2. Review all loan decisions made during the 11-month period to identify affected applicants and measure the full scope of disparate impact.
3. Retrain the model using a reweighted dataset with zip code and employment sector features either removed or constrained to ensure fairness.
4. Require quarterly fairness audits using demographic parity metrics (equal approval rates across groups) and equalized odds metrics (equal true positive and false positive rates) before any future model deployment.
